summary: Non-custodial DeFi lending protocol with Compound V2 and Compound III markets. Compound has remained operational through several historically significant incidents, including a November 2020 DAI liquidation event, a September 2021 COMP reward-distribution bug, and an August 2022 cETH price-feed freeze.
what_happened: On 2020-11-26, an abrupt DAI price increase on Coinbase Pro triggered approximately 85.2 million DAI of liquidations in Compound's DAI market. On 2021-09-29, a bug introduced through Proposal 62 allowed excessive COMP reward claims, prompting emergency governance patches and temporary restrictions on affected COMP claims. On 2022-08-30, a cETH price-feed upgrade caused a temporary denial of service that effectively froze cETH withdrawals and liquidations until Proposal 119 restored the prior oracle path. Compound continued operating and maintains active lending markets in 2026.
uncertainty_notes: The reviewed incidents have different economic meanings: 2020 liquidations are not equivalent to protocol bad debt, 2021 excess COMP distribution is not customer-principal loss, and the 2022 cETH incident was a temporary market-specific availability failure. CYA does not infer a universal compensation or recovery percentage across them.
notes: DeFi backfill record. Historical incidents are modeled separately while current platform status remains active.
